dedupe_keys.name: hybrid network and agent based pedestrian movement model fraunhofer chalmers gothenburg

description: This hybrid model, published by Anita Ullrich, Franziska Hunger, Ioanna Stavroulaki and colleagues from the Fraunhofer-Chalmers Research Centre, Chalmers University, Industrial Path Solutions, Viscando, Liljewall arkitekter and RISE in Frontiers in Built Environment on 7 November 2024, links two pedestrian models into one workflow for urban planners. Contents: a network model predicts aggregated pedestrian flows on street segments at city scale, and its origin-destination shares become boundary conditions for an agent-based model that simulates individual walkers in outdoor spaces. Coverage: applied to a pedestrian precinct in central Gothenburg, Sweden, and compared with real-world measurements, with reasonable agreement at both scales. Format and access: described in an open-access article with parameter tables; no public code release was found. Licence and cost: article free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: one precinct and one time window, and the agent software comes from the industrial partner. It lets planners test design scenarios, flow distributions and movement restrictions, so it can support capacity planning and network flow models of walking, including closures or crowding after a disruption. It relates to the Jülich pedestrian dynamics archive and the Melbourne pedestrian counts in the catalogue.
